explanation: The negative pole is the descriptive end of a lexical dial whose verified positive end is domain-classifying vocabulary: it fires on the ordinary word that says what something is like - a qualitative adjective, participle or abstract noun in modifier or head position of a noun phrase ("some practical steps", "the affected device", "a physical presence", "this unseen supply", "the foreign land") - in general-audience advice, explanation and news prose about typical or hypothetical cases. Put an identifying or classifying word in the same slot instead (medical, clinical, technical, specific, useful, essential, actual, real, true) and the pole drops to zero while the positive pole takes over, so a word fires here only when its sentence uses it to describe rather than to classify, identify, or assert established fact.
